articles.title: Scopeabout
articles.summary: This article details a "scopeabout" tour of significant astronomical sites and observatories across New South Wales, Australia, following the 2000 South Pacific Star Party. The tour covers a range of facilities from amateur club observatories and historical sites to major professional optical and radio observatories like Siding Spring, Parkes, Narrabri, and Mount Stromlo, as well as the NASA Deep Space Communication Complex. It highlights Australia's rich astronomical landscape, offering insights into research, public engagement, and dark-sky observing opportunities.
keywords: Astronomical Society of New South Wales (ASNSW)

articles.title: Astrocon 2000 July 19-22
articles.summary: Astrocon 2000, the 54th annual convention of the Astronomical League and several other prominent astronomy organizations, is set to take place from July 19-22 at the Holiday Inn Ventura Beach Resort. Hosted by the Ventura County Astronomical Society, this significant conference for the new millennium will feature a program of lectures, workshops, and field trips, including tours of Mt. Wilson and JPL, welcoming both members and non-members.

articles.title: Follow the Dots to a Secret Project
articles.summary: The article details a personal lunar observation by Dave North, highlighting what he calls a 'secret project'—a seemingly undocumented, buried extension of Rima Conon that appears to connect with the Bradley rille complex and Rima Archimedes through the Apennine Mountains. He encourages other amateur astronomers to observe this phenomenon around May 10th and contribute to the discussion, emphasizing the potential for discovery in overlooked lunar areas. The author speculates on its geological significance and invites community input on this peculiar formation.

articles.title: Swift and Bright
articles.summary: The Eta Aquarids meteor shower, active from April 19 to May 28 and associated with comet 1P/Halley, offers moonlit-free viewing for observers this month. Known for swift, bright meteors that frequently leave persistent trains, this shower has a ZHR of 60 and is also a good radio shower for both hemispheres, despite its radiant rising only an hour or two before dawn in mid-northern latitudes.

articles.title: Our First Messier Marathon
articles.summary: The article presents two distinct amateur astronomy experiences. Bob Havner details a successful Messier Marathon with Len Bradley on April 1, 2000, where they observed 98 Messier objects, exceeding their goal. Separately, Norman Wild reviews the construction and features of a new AstroSystems Telekit telescope mount, praising its design improvements and functionality despite a six-month wait for components.

articles.title: Pinnacles Starry Night Programs
articles.summary: Pinnacles National Monument will host a series of 'Starry Night' astronomy programs on the east side of the park this spring, specifically on May 5th and June 2nd. These events will offer great views of the night sky, inviting amateur astronomers with their own telescopes to participate. Visitors should dress warmly, note the east side-only access, and call ahead for weather-related cancellations.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article for May 2000 discusses the challenging conditions for observing most easily visible planets, as many are positioned too close to the Sun in both evening and morning skies. It highlights specific close conjunctions of Jupiter with Venus and Saturn as difficult but observable events, recommending binoculars for location. For late-evening observers, the outer planets—Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto—are presented as the primary targets, with advice on finding Pluto near opposition.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: Don Machholz's "Comet Comments" reports ongoing comet discoveries by SOHO and LINEAR, noting the lack of bright comets this month and tempering expectations for Comet LINEAR (C/1999 S4). The article also discusses the declining rate of visual comet discoveries by amateurs due to automated programs. Machholz announces this as his final column after 21 years, citing the internet's ability to provide more timely news.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The SJAA Loaner Scope Status document provides a detailed update on the availability and current loans of telescopes to its members. It categorizes scopes as immediately available, recently loaned with due dates, or on extended loan/under repair, including descriptions and current custodians/borrowers. SJAA members interested in borrowing a scope can contact Mike Koop, with a waiting list provided for popular items.
